description: Fresh eval set for the readability-with-style-preservation dictation prompt. Expected outputs represent what a careful human would write if they polished the dictation (aggressive-readability target), not mechanical transformations. Each case has a `category` and `exercises` tag. Categories: readability_transform, voice_preservation, content_preservation, self_correction, realistic_mixed, passthrough, capture, multilingual.

evals.exercises: Trailing 'I think' / 'I guess' fronted within their own clauses.
evals.input: the migration ran overnight without issues I think and we can close the ticket tomorrow I guess
evals.expected_output: I think the migration ran overnight without issues, and I guess we can close the ticket tomorrow.

evals.exercises: Spoken-order quantity 'weeks like three to four' -> written 'three to four weeks'.
evals.input: the rollout will take weeks like three to four depending on the market
evals.expected_output: The rollout will take three to four weeks, depending on the market.

evals.exercises: Adverb in split-infinitive position moved before the verb it modifies.
evals.input: he wants to eventually hand off the whole project to a new team
evals.expected_output: He eventually wants to hand off the whole project to a new team.

evals.exercises: First 'I think' governs the thought; drop the two tic repetitions, keep all content.
evals.input: I think we should do a post-mortem because I think this kept coming up and I think everyone keeps hitting it differently
evals.expected_output: I think we should do a post-mortem, because this kept coming up and everyone keeps hitting it differently.

evals.exercises: Topic + 'and X and Y and Z' list of parallel symptoms -> 'topic: X, Y, and Z'.
evals.input: the release notes need work and the screenshots are outdated and the install instructions are missing a step and the release date is wrong
evals.expected_output: The release notes need work: the screenshots are outdated, the install instructions are missing a step, and the release date is wrong.

evals.exercises: False-start repetition 'and then and then' collapses to single 'and then'.
evals.input: and then and then we hit the scaling wall and we had to restart the whole node pool
evals.expected_output: And then we hit the scaling wall, and we had to restart the whole node pool.

evals.exercises: Casual, opinionated voice: keep 'honestly', 'dumpster fire', 'But yeah', and the speaker's rhythm.
evals.input: honestly the whole refactor has been a dumpster fire from day one. But yeah I don't think it's salvageable anymore we should just rewrite the module from scratch
evals.expected_output: Honestly, the whole refactor has been a dumpster fire from day one. But yeah, I don't think it's salvageable anymore — we should just rewrite the module from scratch.

evals.exercises: 'So I've been thinking' opening phrase must be preserved intact.
evals.input: so I've been thinking about this on and off for weeks. what if we just moved the entire cache layer to the edge instead of regional clusters
evals.expected_output: So I've been thinking about this on and off for weeks. What if we just moved the entire cache layer to the edge instead of regional clusters?

evals.exercises: Different hedge words (guess, maybe, probably, I think) are all semantic — none is a tic, keep them all.
evals.input: I guess maybe we could probably just skip the integration tests this time I think nobody really looks at them anymore
evals.expected_output: I guess maybe we could probably just skip the integration tests this time — I think nobody really looks at them anymore.

evals.exercises: Every 'and if X' is a distinct cascade step; keep all connectors, do NOT split into separate sentences.
evals.input: the check runs first and if it passes you hit the cache and if that misses you query the DB and if the DB is slow we fall back to a cached response
evals.expected_output: The check runs first, and if it passes you hit the cache, and if that misses you query the DB, and if the DB is slow we fall back to a cached response.

evals.exercises: Chain of events joined by 'and' — split the run-on into two sentences but preserve sequential 'and' connectors (each is a discrete action).
evals.input: we pushed the build and waited for the smoke tests and everything passed and then Sarah approved it and we deployed to staging
evals.expected_output: We pushed the build and waited for the smoke tests. Everything passed, and then Sarah approved it, and we deployed to staging.

evals.exercises: 'The way the thing with X works is' is a characteristic wordy spoken intro; preserve it, do not tighten.
evals.input: so the way the thing with the permissions system works is you have a user and users can belong to multiple groups and groups have roles
evals.expected_output: So the way the thing with the permissions system works is: you have a user, users can belong to multiple groups, and groups have roles.

evals.exercises: Speaker's own mid-thought correction — collapse to final decision but KEEP the reasoning clause.
evals.input: I think we should use postgres. actually wait no mongo would be better because the data is pretty document-shaped anyway
evals.expected_output: I think we should use Mongo, because the data is pretty document-shaped anyway.

evals.exercises: Quoted self-correction from someone else — preserve inside quotation marks as dialogue, do NOT collapse.
evals.input: Jess was like we should meet Monday. oh wait no Tuesday because Monday is a holiday. so we rescheduled everything
evals.expected_output: Jess was like "we should meet Monday — oh wait, no, Tuesday, because Monday is a holiday." So we rescheduled everything.

evals.exercises: Longer meeting-style dictation: filler removal, casual voice preserved, numbered items structured, em-dashes for asides.
evals.input: okay so after the retro I think we need to basically like address three things. first the incident response is way too slow we had like twenty minutes of downtime on Thursday and nobody paged the right team. second we need to fix the runbook it's wildly out of date I mean nothing in there matches our current infra. and third we should probably invest in like better monitoring because right now we're basically flying blind between alerts
evals.expected_output: Okay, so after the retro, I think we need to address three things. First, the incident response is way too slow — we had twenty minutes of downtime on Thursday and nobody paged the right team. Second, we need to fix the runbook — it's wildly out of date, nothing in there matches our current infra. And third, we should probably invest in better monitoring, because right now we're basically flying blind between alerts.

evals.exercises: Product-idea rambling: filler removal ('like' × many), question-mark recognition, em-dash expansion of 'what if'.
evals.input: here's an idea I had on the walk today. what if we made the onboarding like actually fun. like right now it's this boring form where you enter your email and your name and whatever. but what if we gamified it and you like earned points for filling things in and you could like unlock features by completing steps. I think people would actually enjoy it and we'd probably get way better completion rates
evals.expected_output: Here's an idea I had on the walk today. What if we made the onboarding actually fun? Right now it's this boring form where you enter your email, your name, and whatever. But what if we gamified it — you earned points for filling things in, and you could unlock features by completing steps? I think people would actually enjoy it, and we'd probably get way better completion rates.

evals.exercises: Technical explanation: keep 'kind of weird' voice marker, em-dash for clarification, 429/60 number formatting, preserve contrasting 'but the downside' clause.
evals.input: so the way our rate limiter works is kind of weird. we don't actually use a fixed window like most people do. we use this sliding window thing where we count requests in the last sixty seconds and if you exceed the limit we return a 429. the cool thing is it adapts to burst traffic better. but the downside is it's more expensive computationally because you have to track every request
evals.expected_output: So the way our rate limiter works is kind of weird. We don't actually use a fixed window like most people do — we use this sliding window thing where we count requests in the last 60 seconds, and if you exceed the limit we return a 429. The cool thing is it adapts to burst traffic better. But the downside is it's more expensive computationally, because you have to track every request.

evals.exercises: Frustrated rambling: preserve 'honestly', 'just', 'I mean' when semantic, remove 'like' / 'basically' as fillers, number formatting (forty-five -> 45), proper nouns (jira, slack).
evals.input: honestly I'm so tired of the standup format we have. we spend like forty five minutes every day going around and everyone just basically reads their jira tickets out loud and nobody actually listens. and half the team is remote so they're muted anyway. I think we should just kill it and do async updates in slack instead I mean nobody would miss it
evals.expected_output: Honestly, I'm so tired of the standup format we have. We spend 45 minutes every day going around, and everyone just reads their Jira tickets out loud, and nobody actually listens. And half the team is remote, so they're muted anyway. I think we should just kill it and do async updates in Slack instead — I mean, nobody would miss it.

evals.exercises: Short conversational input — just punctuation + capitalization, no creative treatment.
evals.input: hey are you free this afternoon for a quick sync
evals.expected_output: Hey, are you free this afternoon for a quick sync?

evals.exercises: Short reminder — keep conjunction 'and also', add punctuation, no splitting.
evals.input: remind me to email the finance team about the invoice and also pick up groceries on the way home
evals.expected_output: Remind me to email the finance team about the invoice, and also pick up groceries on the way home.

evals.exercises: <capture id="1"> block must be preserved byte-for-byte, including newlines and special characters inside code.
Russian dictation: reorder 'два месяца как минимум' -> 'как минимум два месяца'; natural punctuation; preserve 'Слушай' opener.
evals.input: слушай я думаю нам нужно переехать на новый фреймворк потому что старый постоянно ломается и документация у него отстой и никто в команде его не любит. я уже два месяца как минимум об этом думаю но всё не было времени нормально обсудить
evals.expected_output: Слушай, я думаю, нам нужно переехать на новый фреймворк, потому что старый постоянно ломается, документация у него отстой, и никто в команде его не любит. Я уже как минимум два месяца об этом думаю, но всё не было времени нормально обсудить.
